svg.text: Every top-level directory, classified before anything was touched
KEEP
the chat core, the client, the schemas, the tool-calling layer, config, the cache
STRIP
the search engine, reopened later, see below
REMOVED
the Kubernetes charts, and the whole CI directory: 45 files, 20+ workflows
publishing to registries under upstream's owner and secrets
DEFER
the end-to-end suite, most of it exercises surfaces being withdrawn
REVERSED
"strip the tracing directory", after measuring, it is not a directory
at all: the instrumentation is a dependency. Pinned off instead.
Five inherited defaults that pointed out of the customer's network
In a product whose entire premise is that nothing leaves it.
Three hosted providers, shipped switched on
Their keys read
user_provided
, which is not a placeholder: a non-empty value means
"this endpoint exists", so it appears in the interface and asks each person for their own key.
An embeddings provider named after a vendor
The name is the wire format, not a destination, and the base URL defaulted to empty, so
switching on file upload would have sent every document's text to that vendor.
A skills subsystem that fetches from a public code host
236 test files in the production image, one carrying a published encryption key
Release workflows publishing images under somebody else's account
How each was found
By building the image and looking, not by reading the Dockerfile. By running the guard against a
built container, not by reasoning about what it covers. Two of the five were invisible in the diff.
